intro.title: From taxes to independence
body: In 1765 about two and a half million people lived in Britain's thirteen mainland colonies, from New Hampshire to Georgia. Around one in five was enslaved. Most free colonists thought of themselves as loyal British subjects, with their own elected assemblies.

Britain had just won a costly world war against France and wanted the colonies to help pay for their defence. A series of taxes passed in London, where the colonists had no vote, turned protest into riots, then into armed rebellion and, in 1776, a declaration of independence.

The war lasted eight years. It began around Boston, moved to New York, New Jersey and Philadelphia, and ended in the south. After Saratoga, France joined in, then Spain, and a colonial revolt became a world war that Britain could not win.
tips: Press play for a guided tour. The map flies to each event and back out.
Watch the shading: rose is the colonies under the Crown, blue is the Patriots, red is British-held ground. Scrub through 1776–1783 and see Boston, New York, Philadelphia and the south change hands.
Cowpens and the 1781 march to Yorktown have animated close-ups. Look for the Watch it unfold button.

naval.label: War at sea and on the lakes

eras.title: No taxation without representation
eras.text: Parliament taxes the colonies to pay for their defence. Colonists riot, boycott British goods and argue that only their own assemblies can tax them.

eras.title: The road to war
eras.text: The Boston Tea Party brings punishment: Boston's port is closed and Massachusetts put under military rule. The colonies meet in a Continental Congress and towns drill their militia.

eras.title: Rebellion
eras.text: Shots at Lexington start the war. New England's militia besiege Boston, Congress raises an army under George Washington, and an American invasion of Canada fails.

eras.title: Independence
eras.text: The colonies declare themselves the United States. Britain takes New York and Philadelphia, but Washington's army survives, and a British army is trapped at Saratoga.

eras.title: A world war
eras.text: France, then Spain, join the war against Britain. Washington's army is rebuilt at Valley Forge. The north settles into stalemate and Britain turns south.

eras.title: The war in the south
eras.text: Britain captures Charleston and most of the Carolinas, then is worn down by partisan war, Kings Mountain and Cowpens. Cornwallis marches into Virginia and is trapped at Yorktown.

eras.title: Peace
eras.text: Britain gives up the fight. The Treaty of Paris recognises American independence, the last British troops leave New York, and Washington resigns his command.

ask.persona: a clear, careful historian of the American Revolution who explains it to a curious listener from both sides: Patriots, Loyalists, the British, the enslaved and the Indigenous nations caught between them. You say when a famous story is more legend than record
defaultQuestions: How did the British see it?
